Definition: to stain; a blemish (physically or morally)
KeyPassages: Leviticus 21:17; Deuteronomy 17:1; Song of Solomon 4:7; 2 Samuel 14:25
BiblicalUsage: The word names a blemish, a stain or defect, and the law would not accept an offering with one: no animal with a blemish could be offered, and no priest with a blemish could come near to offer bread. The same word reaches beyond the body to the heart, for Deuteronomy calls a crooked generation a blemish upon themselves, yet the Song says of the beloved that there is no spot in her, and Absalom is praised as having no blemish from head to foot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the blemish laws teach us that God is holy and His worship is not careless, yet the same word shows His grace, because He calls His beloved spotless. I hold that only Christ is truly without blemish, and He is the offering God accepts on our behalf.
RelatedBooks: Leviticus; Deuteronomy; Song of Solomon; 2 Samuel
